description: Minimum test count per tier. A suite that shrinks without explanation is a silently disabled suite — a broken include glob drops the unit tier from 1024 tests to 3 and every other gate still passes, because total > 0, failed === 0 and success === true.
howToRaise: Raise a floor in the same commit that adds the tests. Lowering one is also a reviewable diff — state why in the commit message.
establishedBy: PR CI run 19 (run id 30431556718), artifacts `evidence-unit-coverage` / `evidence-security-matrix` / `evidence-integration-tests`, files `test-totals-unit.json`, `test-totals-database.json`, `test-totals-backend.json`, at feature head 8d7bfff09cf914e00ff5ff4587341ece261185c3, started 2026-07-29T07:24:48Z, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest. All three tiers now carry a hosted measurement; none is a local or carried-over figure.
enforcementNote: Only `minTests` is enforced — summarise-vitest.mjs fails a tier that runs fewer. `measured` is provenance: it records what the named run actually observed, so a later reader can see how much headroom a floor had when it was set.

unit.note: Raised from 1000 to 1050. Run 19 measured 1082 on a hosted runner, replacing the local 1024 that established the old floor. The floor keeps roughly 30 tests of headroom for ordinary churn while no longer sitting 82 below the real count, where it could have absorbed an entire deleted test file without complaint.

web.note: RAISED to 4459 by the P1-32 inventory screens on this branch, which added test files for the material requirements panel, the unit conversions screen and the vehicle specification screen and pushed the DECLARED count to 3740 across 162 files, above the previous floor of 3700 - `WTF-08` refused it, as it must. The raise is FORCED, not chosen, from three sides: `WTF-08` refuses a floor beneath cases that physically exist (3740); `WTF-09` refuses a headroom wider than the largest file in the tree (118 declared cases in `delivery.dom.test.tsx`), so with the tier EXECUTING 4559 the floor may not sit below 4441; and `baseline-integrity.test.ts` refuses a headroom under one per cent of the measurement, so it may not sit above 4513. 4459 is the round number inside that window. `measured` and `measuredFiles` move with the floor so that all three describe ONE run - 162 files, 4559 executed, 0 failed. The figures the floor replaces described a 135-file tree executing 3749, which this tree left behind; they were not re-measured when the files were added, which is how the floor came to sit below cases on disk. TRACEABILITY, kept rather than dropped: the last HOSTED measurement this line of figures descends from is 3072 on 114 files, taken on PR #314 by GitHub-hosted PR CI run 33936553547 (`Web quality / web-quality`, artifact `evidence-web-quality`), recorded in the run ledger at b813fd77. See `measurementProvenance`.
web.whatTheHeadroomGuarantees: THE FLOOR DETECTS ANY NET LOSS OF MORE THAN 100 EXECUTED TESTS. That is measured (4559) minus the floor (4459), stated as the bound it actually is and recomputed from those two numbers rather than remembered. The file declaring the most cases declares 118 and EXECUTES 133 (`delivery.dom.test.tsx` - `it.each` is one declaration and many cases), so the headroom sits below both. It does NOT sit below every file: `shell.dom.test.tsx` executes 377, so a bound of 100 is what is claimed here and nothing wider.
web.measuredFilesNote: `measuredFiles` is 162 - physical `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` files under `apps/web/tests`, matching the tier as this branch holds it, and moved with `measured` so the two describe one run. It read 379 once, because `summarise()` populated it from `numTotalTestSuites`, which vitest sets to every `describe` block recursively. `measuredSuites` is retained so a reader comparing against an older artifact can see which number changed meaning rather than assuming the tier shrank.

unitFloorCaveat: The unit floor is deliberately NOT set to the measurement of the run that carries this commit. This change adds twenty tests — eight in tests/ci/dependency-path-proof.test.ts (AR-49), four in the workflow-security rule-registry suite (AR-50), four in tests/ci/baseline-integrity.test.ts covering the baselines established here, and four in tests/ci/documented-counts.test.ts (AR-51) — so the final head measures 1102, not the 1082 recorded above. Setting 1102 as the floor would make it a transcript of the last run rather than a guard, and every future commit would have to move it. 1050 is the guard; 1082 stays as the provenance of run 19. Note that this sentence is itself the kind of hand-written count AR-51 was about, which is why the floor and the provenance figure — the two values anything actually reads — are measured rather than narrated.
